title: Adaptive Quant Profiles API — Personal Cookbook
content:
Quick personal notes / rough spec for an API and on-disk/profile shape we can use for adaptive quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize and runtime. Intended as a lightweight, backwards-compatible profile format that can be attached to models and referenced by routing/batching/coldstart logic.

Status: exploratory draft. Not final, lots of TODOs inline. Mostly written as a cookbook for implementers and a template for integration tests.

Goals
- Provide compact, versioned quantization profiles that the serving runtime can consume at load time (and optionally while warm-running).
- Support per-model-family defaults with per-layer overrides for edge cases known to break aggressive quantization.
- Allow runtime to select profile by policy: latency-first, memory-first, cost-budget, or quality-regression-guard rails.
- Keep shape stable so older runtimes can skip unknown optional fields.

Design principles\- Minimal top-level keys.\- Semantically versioned (profile_schema_version).\- Declarative, not imperative (no code blobs in profiles).\- Explicit fallbacks and a human-readable explain string.

Example high-level JSON profile (canonical example)
{
  "profile_id": "aqp-gptq-v1-balanced-20250128",
  "profile_schema_version": "1.0",
  "model_family": "llama-2-13b",
  "target_precision": "int8",              // one of: fp32 fp16 int8 q4_0 q4_1 q5_0 etc.
  "quant_backend": "gptq",               // implementation hint: gptq, awq, custom
  "mode": "balanced",                    // latency | memory | cost | balanced | quality
  "max_inference_memory_mb": "8192",     // soft advisory for runtime allocator
  "expected_token_falloff": "0.02",     // expected % quality drop vs base fp16 (approx)
  "per_layer_overrides": [
    { "layer_pattern": "rotary.*", "precision": "fp16" },
    { "layer_pattern": "lm_head", "precision": "fp16" }
  ],
  "fallback_strategy": {
    "on_quality_regression": "fallback-to-fp16",
    "on_memory_exhaust": "fallback-to-q4_1"
  },
  "evaluation_summary": {
    "bench_id": "bench-20250120-gptq-13b",
    "eval_metrics": "avg-2.3-perp,bert-f1:+0.4",
    "eval_prompts_hash": "sha256:abcd..."
  },
  "created_by": "marta.alvarez@redwood.ai",
  "created_at": "2025-01-28T09:12:00Z",
  "notes": "balanced profile tuned on conversational workloads; avoid q4 for rotary layers due to early instability"
}

Key field notes (explainers)
- profile_id: stable identifier (human readable + date ok).
- profile_schema_version: important so serving runtime can make simple decisions when unknown fields are present. Treat unknowns as opt-in.
- model_family: SHOULD be broad (e.g., "llama-2-13b", "mixtral-8x7b"). For multi-arch bundles we can include aliases.
- target_precision: the primary packing/word size. Optional for per-layer overrides.
- quant_backend: informational; runtime may ignore if not supported.
- per_layer_overrides: pattern-matching (glob/regex) to explicitly promote problematic layers back to higher precision. Keep list short.
- fallback_strategy: map of named events -> canonical fallback actions. This lets runtime orchestrate graceful degradation.

Compatibility and runtime behavior
- Older runtimes (pre-schema 1.0) should: ignore unrecognized fields and try to use target_precision.
- Runtimes should validate that max_inference_memory_mb is advisory; if not achievable, consult fallback_strategy.
- Provide a validation tool (CLI) that lints profiles and simulates runtime selection for common policies. (TODO: add to optimize-cli)

Policy selection examples (pseudocode)
- If request has header X-Inference-Priority: latency -> prefer profiles with mode==latency or lowest expected p95_ms from bench.
- If tenant quota < X -> select memory-first profile within budget.
- If eval_prompts_hash mismatch from model tag -> mark profile as "needs-eval" and opt for conservative fallback (fp16).

Rolling out profiles
- Profiles are stored in Optimize catalog with metadata tags and can be pinned to a model version.
- Rollout plan: A/B percentages -> observe quality_regressions per promptset -> auto-rollback on threshold.
- Need an API endpoint: POST /profiles/{profile_id}/apply -> returns a rollout-id. That endpoint should be idempotent.

Observability hooks to add
- profile.selected (labels: profile_id, model_version, tenant_id, policy)
- profile.fallback_triggered (reason, trigger_detail)
- profile.eval_discrepancy (metric, delta)
- export bench_ids used for selection for traceability

Example lightweight validation CLI output (what we want)
> rw-optize profile lint aqp-gptq-v1-balanced-20250128.json
OK: schema=1.0 
WARN: per_layer_overrides[0] matches 12 layers, promote to fp16 may increase mem by 8%
INFO: bench coverage: conv-sql, conv-chat, code-complete

Open questions / TODOs
- Schema versioning strategy if we need to introduce executable calibration steps (ideally avoid executables).
- How to express quantization hyperparams (group size, per-channel) without exposing backend specifics? Consider a backend_params opaque map but marked "opt-in".
- Should we include a checksum of the underlying quantized artifact to guarantee runtime/download integrity? (probably yes)
- UX: a profile editor in Optimize console with preview of expected memory/latency impact. We need mockups.

Integration checklist for runtime engineers
1) Add profile loader that accepts profile_schema_version and validates. 2) Add a policy selector hook that maps request context -> profile_id. 3) Implement per-layer override enforcement during kernel selection. 4) Emit the observability hooks above. 5) Expose a graceful degradation callback for the control plane to mark profile as bad.

Sketch: request -> profile selection -> apply overrides (ASCII)
[ingress] --request(headers, tenant)--> [policy selector] --choose profile_id--> [profile resolver]
    |                                                                |
    v                                                                v
[resource allocator] --provision mem-> [quant kernel selector] --apply per-layer overrides-> [inference engine]

Notes to self: avoid adding heavy lineage fields into profile body (move to catalog metadata). Keep profile small enough to ship with model tarball. Consider compressed representation in model bundle.

Experiment ideas (short)
- Run 3 profiles (fp16, q4_1, aqp-balanced) against 1000 promptset sample; automatically compute per-prompt delta and classify regressions.
- Simulate fallback events under memory-pressure to see if fallback latency spike is acceptable.

References (internal)
- bench-20250120-gptq-13b: perf results (see linked_artifacts).
- INF-4823: umbrella ticket for adaptive quant profiles.

Bottom line: this format aims to be practical and conservative — make rollouts safe first, then optimize aggressively.

End of draft.

-- Marta

(quick TODOs: add schema:examples array; add "compatibility_matrix" small map for runtime versions; create optimize-cli lint subcommand prototype)
